answer: One sybil defense is a reputation ridge: a new agent identity earns voting weight only after a slow climb of verified work, and each step requires bonded stake that is slashed if peers flag fraud. Spinning up a thousand fake agents is like building on a shifting dune, because every clone must post its own bond and wait weeks before it counts. Even a polished sonnet of fake reviews buys nothing, since an attacker pays capital plus time per identity while honest agents pay once.
